inputs.share_count_basis: 396,413,753 common shares issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 interim, note on share capital). No options/RSUs or convertibles disclosed; diluted EPS reported as N/A, so basic = fully diluted. Held flat: no SBC, no buybacks, no equity raises since FY2018.

Parity check vs the TSX line: CGG.TO CAD 38.54 / USDCAD 1.4137 (Yahoo CAD=X, 2026-10-16 close) = US$27.26 vs 2099.HK HK$214.0 / 7.8479 = US$27.27 -- ties to 0.04%, confirming rate, direction and quote basis.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, so USD-built rate: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.05 x 5.0% ERP = 9.6%, + ~0.5pp for PRC/Tibet sovereign-regulatory exposure (expropriation/permitting is not a commodity-path risk the scenarios carry) = 10.0%. Company is net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. Same 10.0% in all three scenarios: commodity-price and operational-disruption risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities US$14.0m (1.5 current + 12.5 non-current at 2026-06-30) included in total_debt; lease principal (~US$0.5m/yr) NOT deducted from flows. Right-of-use and land-use-right payments (US$17.7m FY2025, US$5.1m H1 FY2026) are investing outflows and are carried inside the capex path.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is the CJV partner's 3.5% of the CSH Mine only (Jiama is 100%). Flows are consolidated 100%; NCI deducted once in the equity_bridge at a value of US$35m (~3.5% of the CSH contribution to EV; book NCI US$30.1m at 2026-06-30). H1 FY2026 NCI share of profit was 0.9% of group, consistent.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with the cyclical / non-US adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). A producing two-mine miner is an operating company whose value is a cash-flow stream, so owner-FCF applies; no bank/REIT/NAV row fits. Resource-specific treatment is carried INSIDE the drivers rather than by switching model: (1) the revenue path is built bottom-up as volume x a normalising commodity price deck per scenario (not extrapolated from the FY2025/H1 FY2026 price peak); (2) CSH open-pit depletion is modelled explicitly (0.29 Moz open-pit reserve at 2025-12-31, ~2-3 years) with the underground transition as a base/bull assumption; (3) the terminal value uses a low terminal growth (0-1%) and a 8-11x cap because Jiama's P&P reserve (336.8 Mt at 0.60% Cu, ~23 years at the 14.4 Mtpa permitted rate) is finite -- a 23-year annuity is ~86% of a perpetuity at 10%. TERM DEPOSITS: added to cash (US$403.8m at 2026-06-30, current assets, bank deposits that the company rolls into and out of cash -- US$261m withdrawn in H1 FY2026); excluding them would understate net cash by ~HK$8/share. Cash = 586.4 cash & equivalents + 403.8 term deposits = 990.2. Restricted bank balances (43.5) added separately in the bridge against the environmental rehabilitation provision (97.6). Debt = borrowings 169.1 + 264.9 + entrustment loan payable to related party 29.4 + leases 14.0 = 477.3 (the company's own 'borrowings of US$463.3m' figure is borrowings + entrustment loan). TIMING: the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet already contains H1 FY2026 cash generation, and year 1 of the projection is full-year FY2026, so the H1 FY2026 owner FCF (US$523m) is deducted in the bridge to avoid counting it twice; this is equivalent to valuing off the Dec-2025 net cash less the US$186m FY2025 dividend paid in H1. Year-1 (FY2026) is discounted a full year although ~2.5 months remain -- a small conservative bias. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position null. Buybacks: none ever; flat count is the actual history, not a convention. Interest income (US$8.7m FY2025) stripped from last_fcf because the cash and term deposits that earn it are added to EV; the FVTOCI stake in China Nonferrous Mining (1258.HK, 2.03%) is added at fair value and its dividend income (~US$3m/yr) is excluded from EBITDA (it sits in other income).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (reference only -- the forward path is built from volumes x commodity price deck, not from a historical CAGR)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.9% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 33.1%: diverges far more than 30%. EPS and FCF CAGRs are end-point artefacts of a commodity-price peak (FY2025) measured from a trough-ish base (FY2020) and a mine suspension (FY2023 owner FCF -US$63m); none is a usable forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs to FY2025. Owner FCF = reported FCF - interest income (SBC zero): FY2020 106.4, FY2022 398.8, FY2025 631.4. Owner-FCF CAGR is only marginally below reported (interest income small). Revenue swung 1,105 (FY2022) -> 459 (FY2023, Jiama suspended after the Guolanggou tailings overflow) -> 757 -> 1,310 (FY2025) -> H1 FY2026 914 on near-record gold and a copper rally.

base.growth_rationale: Revenue = volume x price deck. FY2026: H1 actual 914 + H2 ~846 (gold spot US$4,187 vs H1 realised 4,703; CSH open-pit suspended since 22-May slope event, processing stockpiles) = ~1,760, inside guidance (Cu 140-149 Mlb, Au 141-159 koz, Ag 4.2-4.8 Moz). Deck normalises to a mid-cycle by FY2029: realised copper US$4.9 -> 4.6 -> 4.4/lb (Jiama realised runs ~75-80% of LME on concentrate terms), gold US$4,000 -> 3,700 -> 3,400/oz, silver 50 -> 45 -> 40, then +2%/yr nominal. Volumes: Jiama at 34k tpd through FY2027, 44k tpd from FY2028 on the Youlongbu tailings facility (guided end-2027), +25% metal; CSH open pit 80 -> 65 -> 45 -> 25 -> 20 koz as the 0.29 Moz reserve depletes, underground ramp 40 koz FY2031, 60 koz FY2032.
base.margin_rationale: Cash cost build: CSH ~US$1,300-1,700/oz rising with depth; Jiama ~US$2.45-2.60/lb copper (H1 FY2026 cash production cost US$2.48/lb before by-product credit) on rising tonnage; G&A/resource tax/other ~US$90-110m. Costs inflate 3%/yr against a 2% price escalator, so margin drifts from 60% at mid-cycle to 57% by FY2035 (vs 55.5% FY2025 actual and 41-44% in FY2021-22 at much lower gold).
base.capex_rationale: Youlongbu tailings facility and Jiama capacity restoration (FY2027 peak ~US$220m), CSH open-pit-to-underground conversion (FY2028-30), then sustaining ~9.5% of revenue matched to D&A in the terminal year. H1 FY2026 cash capex was only US$28m, so FY2026 is held near 6.8%.
base.tax_rationale: Tibet western-development preferential rate 15% (FY2025 effective ~16%); stepped to 17% from FY2031 for PRC dividend withholding on upstreamed profit and the risk that the preferential regime (extended to 2030) is not renewed in full.

bull.growth_rationale: Near-spot deck held: realised copper ~US$5.4/lb (LME spot US$6.56), gold US$4,200-4,300, silver US$55. Youlongbu on time, Jiama permitted rate raised and back to 50k tpd by FY2029 with high-grade underground blending (the June-2026 reserve upgrade supports this); CSH underground in production from FY2030 at 50-70 koz.

bear.growth_rationale: Deck reverts hard: realised copper US$4.4 -> 4.0 -> 3.6/lb, gold US$3,600 -> 3,100 -> 2,700, silver 42 -> 35 -> 30 by FY2029. Youlongbu slips a year (44k tpd only from FY2029); CSH underground not sanctioned, open pit exhausted by FY2029 (CSH revenue to zero from FY2030). Implicitly carries a partial-year disruption of the 2023-24 kind via the lower volumes.

scenario_narratives.base: Gold and copper come off their 2025-26 highs to a still-elevated mid-cycle (realised Cu ~US$4.4/lb, gold ~US$3,400/oz by FY2029). Jiama steps up to 44k tpd when the Youlongbu tailings facility commissions at end-2027 and runs on a ~23-year reserve; CSH's open pit runs down over 2026-2030 after the May-2026 slope event, with the underground conversion rebuilding output to ~60 koz by FY2032. Margins settle near 57-60%, capex peaks on the tailings dam and the CSH underground, and the company stays net cash. The base case is deliberately not a spot-price case: it is what the mines are worth if commodity prices behave like commodities.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prices stay near spot (copper LME ~US$6.5/lb, gold above US$4,000) on electrification/AI copper demand and central-bank gold buying; Jiama's June-2026 reserve upgrade turns into a permitted-rate increase and a return to the 50k tpd design capacity by FY2029; CSH underground delivers from FY2030. Operating leverage keeps EBITDA margins in the mid-60s and the state-owned parent's support keeps permitting smooth. This is roughly the case today's price is paying for.
scenario_narratives.bear: A commodity reversal (copper realised US$3.6/lb, gold US$2,700) meets the asset concentration the company has already demonstrated twice: Youlongbu slips, the CSH underground is not sanctioned and the open pit is exhausted by FY2029, and Tibet tax preferences lapse. Margins compress to ~50% on a largely fixed cost base. The company remains solvent and net cash, so this is a value case, not a survival case -- but a further tailings or slope incident (2023-24 Jiama, 2026 CSH) would push results below even this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: two-mine concentration with two geotechnical shutdowns in three years (Jiama 2023-24, CSH May-2026) and a deck still well above long-run prices. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs spot commodity prices to persist AND a Tibet permitted-rate increase AND an on-time CSH underground, three independent things. Base 50% is the normalising-deck, guided-expansion path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the mines at a normalising commodity deck, not at the peak. FY2025 and H1 FY2026 earnings are a function of near-record gold and a copper rally; the base case lets prices mean-revert to an elevated mid-cycle, models CSH open-pit depletion explicitly, and caps the terminal value at 8-11x with near-zero terminal growth because Jiama's reserve is finite. On that basis the share price sits close to the bull case: the market is capitalising something near spot prices.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commodity deck: every US$0.25/lb of realised copper is ~US$35-45m of annual revenue at 44k tpd, nearly all of it margin
Geotechnical/tailings incidents at a two-mine company (Jiama 2023-24 suspension cut FY2023 revenue 58%; CSH open-pit suspended since 22-May-2026)
Youlongbu tailings facility timing (guidance moved from H1 2027 to end-2027 between the FY2025 annual and the H1 FY2026 interim) and the Tibet permitted-rate increase
CSH underground conversion: resources, not reserves; capital intensity and timing undisclosed
Tibet preferential tax regime and PRC dividend withholding; related-party dealings with China National Gold
